::: {#rem-score-name}
#### Why the score function is called "score"

The name comes from genetics.
@fisher1935linkage assigned each family in a study of linkage a numerical "score",
the evidence from that family about the linkage parameter.
He compared that scoring rule with an "ideal score",
the derivative of the log of the sampling density,
which is the [score function](#def-score) of these notes
[@wikipedia_informant_function].
For independent observations,
the [log-likelihood](#def-loglik) is a sum over observations,
so its derivative is also a sum, of one contribution per observation.
@rao1948large, who had worked on estimating linkage parameters in Fisher's genetics laboratory,
based a test on these "scores",
the derivatives of the log-likelihood,
and called it a score test [@bera2024score].
The name then spread to the derivative itself.

The word "score" has other meanings in statistics and machine learning.
In particular, these notes call a classifier's raw output the log-odds or linear predictor, never a "score",
so that "score" always means the derivative of the log-likelihood.
:::
